title: Chat API returns 500 due to unhandled JSONDecodeError
description: When llama-server returns a 200 response with malformed or non-JSON body, the Flask proxy crashes while parsing resp.json(), causing an unhandled exception and a generic 500 error. This masks the real issue and makes debugging harder. Additionally, errors during port lookup (e.g., port as non-integer) could cause TypeErrors that also result in 500. Need to add robust error handling around resp.json() and ensure port is cast to int before socket operations.
acceptance_criteria: API no longer crashes on invalid JSON; returns 500 with error details; logs raw response for diagnostics; port converted safely
notes: Root cause: resp.json() can raise JSONDecodeError. Also, check_port_active(port) may receive non-int port causing TypeError. Fix: wrap resp.json() in try-except; ensure port is int before use.
close_reason: Fixed: added JSON error handling and port validation in api_chat; added CSS flex layout for modal-chat to enable proper scrolling and visibility of metrics. All acceptance criteria met.

title: Fix HTTP 500 in /api/chat and chat modal UI issues
Embedded Dolt schema error blocks bead closure
description: Cannot close beads due to Dolt schema mismatch (depends_on_id column missing). This is a known limitation of the embedded Dolt version and cannot be fixed within this workstream. Any bead that attempts to use closure operations will encounter this error. Workaround: avoid bd close; track closure manually outside Beads.

comments.author: Russell Powell
comments.text:
Update: Misdiagnosis Corrected

Original assumption: Embedded Dolt missing depends_on_id column prevented bd close and bd dep add.

Actual cause: Beads application-level validation rule:
- Epics can only block other epics (not tasks)
- Tasks can only block other tasks (not epics)
- Parent/child (containment) is separate from depends_on (blocking)

Evidence:
- bd close operations succeed without error
- bd dep add succeeds when using task→task blocking
- Dolt database schema is healthy; depends_on_id column exists and works

Correct pattern:
- Use bd update --parent for epic→task containment
- Use bd dep add for task→task blocking dependencies

Action: This bead (web-rb7) can be closed or updated as the schema error does not exist. The constraint is behavioral, not structural.

Related refinement: Successfully created full dependency graph for epic web-e7r using proper parent+depends_on relationships.

title: Chat input cleared by periodic refresh
description:
Bug: When user is typing a message in a tile chat, the periodic refresh (every 3s) replaces the tile DOM and clears the input field before the message can be sent. This forces the user to re-type and disrupts the workflow.

Root cause: refresh() sets grid.innerHTML = html which recreates all tile DOM nodes, losing unsaved form state.

Required fix: Preserve chat input values across refresh cycles.

Acceptance criteria:
- User can type a message and take more than 3 seconds to complete without loss
- Input persists through automatic refresh until explicitly sent or cleared
- Existing chat history continues to render correctly after refresh
- No residual event handler issues (existing binding code should work)
- Changes should not break other tile functionality

Background: Chat was recently moved from properties panel to model tiles (bead web-b5e). The tile chat implementation includes:
- Input textarea with id 
- Message history stored in global chatHistory[modelName] array
- Event binding after each refresh in refresh() at lines 2925-2955 in app.py
- Periodic refresh triggered by setInterval(refresh, 3000) plus manual calls

Proposed approach:
1. Before grid.innerHTML assignment, capture current input values by model into a temporary object (modelName -> textarea value)
2. After DOM recreation and event rebinding, restore those values to the appropriate textarea elements
3. Ensure restoration does not interfere with renderChatMessages() or new message addition
4. Verify no duplicate event handlers (current code adds new listeners each refresh; use proper cleanup or idempotent binding)
